themes_detail.label: Homeless crisis spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints surged to 25 THIS WEEK—a 953% increase vs. the 2.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 20.36)—signaling a sudden escalation in street homelessness or crisis interventions in Crown Heights that aligns with repeated community board budget requests for homeless facilities.
evidence: 25 homeless person assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (953% spike, z-score 20.36)
Community board has repeatedly requested expansion of homeless facilities from Department of Homeless Services, indicating chronic underinvestment
Spike is statistically severe—highest z-score among all flagged issues—suggesting a genuine inflection point rather than noise
reporting_angles: Interview DHS and outreach teams on the ground to determine what triggered this week's surge—weather event, shelter closure, policy change, or seasonal migration?
Identify specific blocks/blocks in Crown Heights where complaints cluster and visit to document conditions
Profile residents and local business owners experiencing the impact; connect to broader city homelessness policy debates

themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 72 THIS WEEK—a 292% increase from the 18.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.87)—a sudden and significant disruption to outdoor quality of life in the district.
evidence: 72 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.4 weekly average (292% spike, z-score 4.87)
Mirrors pattern of residential noise complaints (1,240 total over 90 days), indicating noise is a persistent district-wide issue now intensifying outdoors
Timing suggests possible trigger: construction activity, event, or warm weather drawing crowds and outdoor commerce
reporting_angles: Map the 72 complaints geographically—are they concentrated on specific corridors (Atlantic Ave, Flatbush Ave, Prospect Park West) or distributed?
Interview NYPD and 311 dispatchers to identify complaint hotspots and determine if enforcement actions have been taken
Canvass residents and local businesses on what specific noise sources they're reporting (music venues, outdoor dining, construction, vehicles)

themes_detail.label: Non-emergency police calls surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints hit 8 THIS WEEK—a 276% increase from the 2.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.58)—raising questions about what public safety issues are driving escalated 311 calls to NYPD.
evidence: 8 non-emergency police matter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (276% spike, z-score 5.58)
Occurs alongside homeless person assistance spike (25 complaints this week), suggesting possible overlap—e.g., 311 calls for police response to homeless encampments or street crime
Recent Gothamist article (2026-04-21) on NYPD union lawsuit against police watchdog adds local political context to policing tensions in NYC
reporting_angles: FOIL request to NYPD for details on non-emergency call types/locations in CD 308 this week—are they disturbance calls, trespassing, or other categories?
Interview community members and local precinct on whether 311 callers are frustrated with police response times or effectiveness
Explore whether the homeless spike and non-emergency police spike are linked—are complaints about police response to street homelessness driving uptick?

themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards emerging
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO—a 500% increase from the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0)—indicating possible infrastructure or maintenance failures affecting electrical safety.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Timing aligns with spring building activity: 480 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (287 alterations, 97 new buildings), suggesting construction-related electrical work or permit violations
Electrical hazards pose fire and injury risk; spike warrants quick verification
reporting_angles: Request DOB violation and complaint data for CD 308 tied to electrical work in the past 4 weeks; identify problem buildings or contractors
Interview Con Edison on any reported outages, hazardous conditions, or service calls in the district over the same period
Identify the 3 specific buildings with electrical complaints and determine if they're under construction or have code violations

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and facilities neglect
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK—a 184% increase from the 3.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.23)—suggesting accelerating deterioration of public or private infrastructure.
evidence: 11 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (184% spike, z-score 3.23)
Aligns with community board's recurring budget request for 'other cleaning requests' to Sanitation and 'other community board facilities and staff requests' to OMB, indicating systemic underfunding
Occurs alongside other infrastructure spikes (electrical, water/plumbing issues in 90-day data: 682 and 446 complaints respectively)
reporting_angles: Analyze the 11 complaints to determine which facilities are failing most—parks, transit stations, schools, or municipal buildings?
Cross-reference with Parks, Sanitation, and DOE capital plans to assess whether budget requests from community board are being answered
Interview community board members on whether the spike reflects deferred maintenance or new failures
